style: An antique hand-drawn sea chart in ink and wash on aged parchment, its converging sea-lanes, forking channels and dashed return-courses standing in for the essay's funnels, fork and loop.

plates.title: The Chart Of Conscious AI

vignettes.quote: with consciousness comes moral status, the potential for suffering and, perhaps, rights
vignettes.depicts: A small brass clockwork automaton, chained to a post on a rocky shore, wincing as if in pain.
vignettes.title: A MACHINE THAT MIGHT SUFFER

vignettes.quote: a face in a piece of toast or Mother Teresa in a cinnamon bun
vignettes.depicts: A round bun on a plate, its swirled crust forming a faint face, with tiny pilgrim figures on the shore gazing up at it in wonder.
vignettes.title: FACE IN THE BUN

vignettes.quote: The brain is not a Turing machine made of meat.
vignettes.depicts: A brain carved like a cut of meat sitting atop a cluster of broken cogwheels that fail to mesh or turn.
vignettes.title: MEAT, NOT A MACHINE

vignettes.quote: a chatbot called LaMDA. He claimed it was conscious, that it had feelings
vignettes.depicts: A seated engineer leaning toward a glowing console marked only with a single speech-bubble shape, his hand raised in astonishment.
vignettes.title: LEMOINE AND THE CHATBOT

vignettes.quote: more breath than thought and more meat than machine
vignettes.depicts: A figure in a final cove, one side rendered as drifting mist and breath, the other as solid flesh, its edges fading into scattered cogwheels.
vignettes.title: MORE BREATH THAN THOUGHT

plates.prompt: An antique hand-drawn sea chart on aged, browned parchment, rendered in ink and faded wash — sepia, dull teal and tarnished gold, with cracked varnish and soft foxing at the edges. The page reads as a single voyage from top to bottom. At the very top, inside a round cartouche bordered with carved rope, sits a small brass clockwork automaton chained to a post on a rocky shore, wincing in evident distress; lettered beneath in large, clear capitals: A MACHINE THAT MIGHT SUFFER. From this cartouche two dotted rhumb-lines sweep downward and outward like converging sea-lanes. The left lane runs down past a small whirlpool to a shoreline scene: a round bun resting on a plate, its swirled crust forming a faint face, tiny pilgrim figures standing on the beach gazing up at it in wonder; lettered beneath: FACE IN THE BUN. The right lane runs down to a rocky headland where a brain, carved like a cut of meat, sits atop a heap of broken cogwheels that refuse to mesh; lettered beneath: MEAT, NOT A MACHINE. Below both, the lanes pass a coiled, unlettered sea-serpent marking an unnamed hazard, then one channel opens into a small harbor: a seated figure leans toward a glowing console marked only with a plain speech-bubble shape, his hand raised in astonishment; lettered beneath: LEMOINE AND THE CHATBOT. All routes then descend to a final cove at the foot of the chart, where a single figure stands half as drifting mist and breath, half as solid flesh, its outer edge dissolving into loose scattered cogwheels; lettered beneath: MORE BREATH THAN THOUGHT. A long dashed homeward course, drawn like a ship's return route, arcs from this final cove back up the right margin of the chart to the cartouche at the very top, closing the loop. A plain compass rose, soundings, and small ink-drawn sailing ships fill the empty corners of the parchment as unlettered ornament. Lettering beneath each scene is large and easy to read; nothing else on the page carries any words.

plates.title: Why We're Tempted

vignettes.quote: a face in a piece of toast or Mother Teresa in a cinnamon bun
vignettes.depicts: The same bun-with-a-face scene from the overview, set in a round cartouche at the top of the chart as a framing medallion.
vignettes.title: FACE IN THE BUN

vignettes.quote: solving a crossword puzzle, assembling some furniture, navigating a tricky family situation, walking to the shop
vignettes.depicts: A figure at a table solving a crossword, surrounded by half-built furniture and a shopping basket, a montage of ordinary busy tasks.
vignettes.title: CROSSWORD, FURNITURE, SHOP

vignettes.quote: to see things through the lens of being human
vignettes.depicts: A large eye peering through a pair of human-shaped spectacles at the rest of the chart.
vignettes.title: THROUGH A HUMAN LENS

vignettes.quote: on an exponential curve, every point is an inflection point
vignettes.depicts: A steep rising wave-like contour drawn across the chart, a tiny ship climbing it, small flags planted at every point along its length.
vignettes.title: EVERY POINT AN INFLECTION

vignettes.quote: closer to angels and Gods than to other animals, as in the medieval Scala naturae
vignettes.depicts: A tall wooden ladder rising into clouds: humans partway up the rungs, winged figures and radiant gods above, animals clustered below.
vignettes.title: THE LADDER OF NATURE

vignettes.quote: “If you’ve created a conscious machine — it’s not the history of man, that’s the history of Gods.”
vignettes.depicts: Two small figures on a dockside, one gesturing grandly toward a glowing radiant shape, as if performing a god-like act of creation.
vignettes.title: HISTORY OF GODS

vignettes.quote: Nobody, as far as I know, has claimed that DeepMind’s AlphaFold is conscious
vignettes.depicts: Two machines side by side on a dock: a folded-chain shape ignored by passersby, and a glowing chat-console admired by a small crowd.
vignettes.title: ALPHAFOLD IGNORED, CHATBOTS ADORED

vignettes.quote: see a dead relative standing at the foot of the bed
vignettes.depicts: A dim bedroom with a bed, a translucent ghostly figure standing at its foot.
vignettes.title: A GHOST AT THE BEDSIDE

plates.prompt: An antique hand-drawn sea chart, ink and faded wash on aged parchment — sepia, dull teal, tarnished gold — matching the style and palette of a larger chart it belongs to. At the very top of the page, inside a round rope-bordered cartouche, is the round bun on a plate with a faint face in its swirled crust, tiny pilgrim figures on the shore below gazing up at it; lettered beneath: FACE IN THE BUN. This cartouche serves as the frame for everything below it. Directly beneath, the chart proper begins with a harbor scene: a figure at a table solving a crossword, surrounded by half-assembled furniture and a shopping basket; lettered beneath: CROSSWORD, FURNITURE, SHOP. From this harbor the coastline forks into two channels running side by side down the page. The left channel passes first a large eye peering through human-shaped spectacles at the chart around it, lettered THROUGH A HUMAN LENS; then a tall wooden ladder rising into the clouds, humans partway up its rungs, winged god-like figures above, animals below, lettered THE LADDER OF NATURE; then two machines on a dock, one shaped like a folded chain and ignored, the other a glowing console admired by a small crowd, lettered ALPHAFOLD IGNORED, CHATBOTS ADORED; then a dim bedroom with a translucent ghostly figure standing at the foot of a bed, lettered A GHOST AT THE BEDSIDE. The right channel passes a steep rising wave-like contour with a tiny ship climbing it and flags planted along its length, lettered EVERY POINT AN INFLECTION; then a dockside scene of two small figures, one gesturing toward a glowing radiant shape, lettered HISTORY OF GODS. From the final scene of each channel, a dashed line climbs back up the margins of the chart to the cartouche at the top, showing both channels feeding into the same frame. A compass rose and small unlettered ink ships fill empty corners. All titles are lettered large and clear beneath their scenes; nothing else on the page carries any words.

plates.title: Why It's Probably Not There

vignettes.quote: The brain is not a Turing machine made of meat.
vignettes.depicts: The same meat-brain-and-broken-cogwheels scene from the overview, set in a round cartouche at the top of the chart as a framing medallion.
vignettes.title: MEAT, NOT A MACHINE

vignettes.quote: real artificial consciousness is fully off the table
vignettes.depicts: A wooden table at the chart's harbor, a glowing humanoid figure sliding off its edge and falling away into shadow.
vignettes.title: OFF THE TABLE

vignettes.quote: no sharp separation between “mindware” and “wetware” as there is between software and hardware
vignettes.depicts: A computer box cleanly divided by a drawn line into two labeled compartments, beside a brain rendered as one unbroken wet, fleshy mass with no dividing line at all.
vignettes.title: MINDWARE BLEEDS INTO WETWARE

vignettes.quote: two heavy cantilevered balls swing outwards, which in turn closes a valve
vignettes.depicts: A steam engine fitted with a spinning governor mechanism, its two weighted balls swinging outward on rods as a valve closes beside it.
vignettes.title: THE STEAM GOVERNOR

vignettes.quote: into the molecular furnaces of metabolism
vignettes.depicts: A single cell drawn as a small stone furnace with a glowing fire inside its chamber.
vignettes.title: FURNACES OF METABOLISM

vignettes.quote: A simulation of a rainstorm does not make anything actually wet.
vignettes.depicts: A storm cloud rendered as a flat inked diagram above dry, cracked ground, its drawn raindrops never reaching or wetting the earth below.
vignettes.title: A STORM THAT MAKES NOTHING WET

vignettes.quote: progressively replacing brain parts with silicon equivalents that function in exactly the same way
vignettes.depicts: A row of brain slices laid out on a table, each one further along than the last in being replaced by shining silicon fragments.
vignettes.title: SWAPPING NEURONS FOR SILICON

vignettes.quote: associated most closely with the philosopher Nick Bostrom
vignettes.depicts: A robed philosopher figure standing before a large swirling starry orb crossed with fine grid lines, representing a simulated cosmos.
vignettes.title: BOSTROM'S SIMULATED WORLD
